title: Enable partition support in dplyr
description:
Many BigQuery tables are [date-partitioned](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/best-practices-costs#partition_data_by_date), This allows for cheap querying from the BQ console, since users can specify the `_PARTITIONTIME` pseudo column to filter for a date or a range of dates. Here's an example from the [Global Fishing Watch](https://globalfishingwatch.org/data-blog/our-data-in-bigquery/) project:

```
SELECT
  SUM(fishing_hours) AS total_fishing_hours,
  flag
FROM
  [global-fishing-watch:global_footprint_of_fisheries.fishing_effort]
WHERE
  _PARTITIONTIME >= "2016-01-01 00:00:00"
  AND _PARTITIONTIME < "2017-01-01 00:00:00"
GROUP BY
  flag
ORDER BY
  total_fishing_hours DESC
```

Is it possible to support this kind of partitioning in in `bigrquery` / `dplyr`? I've tried to hack the translation using !! but my tidyeval skills failed me.

Thanks for considering.

I have got tons of automation scripts with query_exec() failing. So wondering if there would be fix in the next update or the above roundabout solution is the only way?

title: Use Google Cloud SDK config authentication
description:
Greetings!

I'm trying to get bigrquery working for data scientists at Spotify, inside of a docker image. Here are the constraints:

- Folks love notebooks, so interactive authentication flow is out
- Per company policy, all data queries must executed by individual, so using a service account with `set_service_token(path)` is out

Many other tools and APIs that interact with GCP use Google Cloud SDK credentials. You "login" from the command line, triggering an interactive oauth flow similar to the one in bigrquery.

`gcloud auth login`

You can then see the active account with:
`gcloud config list`

1. Would it be possible for bigrquery to check for authentication here before asking for an interactive flow? This would mirror the behavior that many of google's own tools follow. (I believe the credentials are stored in ~/.config/gcloud/)

2. Some tools only work with application default credentials. That's typically the way you tell an application to use a service account in product. But you can also use it locally - with your personal account instead of a service account. You just do

`gcloud auth application-default login`

and go through the usual flow. This generates a json file in `~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json`. I tried using that with `set_service_token(path)`, but the json key is in a different format than the service account keys use.

Assuming this is a good idea, I'd be happy to hack on this given some direction.

title: Issue flipping priority from Interactive to Batch
description: Has anyone had an issue before flipping the priority from Interactive to Batch? My team and I are trying to read over 100 items from BigQuery at once, each from it's own Kubernetes node. So that obviously goes over the BigQuery 50 request limit in Interactive mode. After switching priority = "INTERACTIVE" to priority = "BATCH" in the API call, the developers who tested the code are telling me that the request is still not being fully served due to the 50 concurrent limit. 50 requests are completed, but the remaining 50 fail. Has anyone seen anything similar to this before, where even after flipping priority that the API call is still being sent as INTERACTIVE? Is there perhaps a better route? It seems as though abstracting this API call out to separate smaller chunks would prove to be more difficult. Please let me know if more information is necessary to help.

title: Long download times for large query results in bigrquery
description:
Our query_exec command is taking 2 hours to download a 27MB dataset (~320K rows) when max_pages is set to Inf and page_size is set to 10K. 

We seem to be having the same issue as this individual: https://community.rstudio.com/t/bigrquery-large-datasets/2632 
They seem to have found that their 1GB file download times went from 1 hour down to 2 mins when they downloaded it as JSON from Google Cloud Storage. 

Theoretically, our dataset streaming down from BigQuery should take just minutes as well.

Given the discrepant times between services for the same dataset, is this a bug or is there a solution to download large datasets from Google BigQuery via bigrquery more quickly?

To clarify: The exact same bigrquery query takes **just minutes to download data in RStudio** but **hours when running the same query in a Jupyter notebook.**

title: User Agent String Does not Follow GPN format
description:
The current package produces a user agent string similar to "bigrquery/0.4.1 httr/1.2.1,gzip(gfe)" which does not follow the user agent compliance with RFC (http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section­5.5.3)

Suggested format
"<prod_name>/ver (GPN:<company name>; <other comments>) <other prod>/ver "*

Example
"Product_A/1.1 (GPN:Partner_ABC; staging) Product_B/1.3
Google­HTTP­Java­Client/1.20.0"

Making this small modification would enable tracking of the use of this package in the Google Cloud Platform.

title: true values convert to FALSE when results are returned to R as tibble
description:
Hey I've noticed while playing around with `v0.4.1.9000` that `true` values in query results seem to be getting converted to `FALSE` when returned to R as a tibble.

I'm having trouble getting a `reprex()` to work but I will explain in detail below how to replicate.

## Ground truth

First here's the query I've been playing around with:

```r
sql <- "SELECT repository.has_downloads, COUNT(*) AS n FROM `publicdata.samples.github_nested` GROUP BY repository.has_downloads"
```

Querying in the BigQuery web UI and via `bq` command returns the ground truth results:

```r
system2('bq', glue::glue("query --use_legacy_sql=false '{sql}'"))

#> +---------------+---------+
#> | has_downloads |    n    |
#> +---------------+---------+
#> |         false |   62368 |
#> |          true | 2222838 |
#> |          NULL |  256433 |
#> +---------------+---------+
```

## Problems

Now when I run this query via the **Low-level API** and **DBI interfaces** I see unexpected behaviour where these `true` values become `FALSE`. Since this query is on a nested field (`repository`) I don't think I can try the **dplyr** interface, but I have another example below where the problem also exists.

### Low-level API

Here's how to replicate the problem when using the Low-level API:

```r
library(bigrquery)
billing <- bq_test_project()

tb <- bq_project_query(billing, sql)
#> Complete
#> Billed: 0 B

bq_table_download(tb, max_results = 10)
#> Downloading 3 rows in 1 pages.
#> # A tibble: 3 x 2                                                                                          
#>   has_downloads       n
#>   <lgl>           <int>
#> 1 FALSE           62368
#> 2 FALSE         2222838
#> 3 NA             256433
```

Note the **TWO FALSE values**. Unusual. I don't know enough C++ to try work out what is happening sorry.

### DBI

Problem also exists in DBI:

```r
library(DBI)
con <- dbConnect(
  bigrquery::bigquery(),
  project = "publicdata",
  dataset = "samples",
  billing = billing
)

res <- dbGetQuery(con, sql)
#> Complete
#> Billed: 0 B
#> Downloading 3 rows in 1 pages.

res
#> # A tibble: 3 x 2
#>   has_downloads       n
#>   <lgl>           <int>
#> 1 FALSE           62368
#> 2 FALSE         2222838
#> 3 NA             256433
```

### dplyr

Here's another query that results in similar issues when using `dplyr`:

```r
library(dplyr)
natality <- tbl(con, "bigquery-public-data.samples.natality")

natality %>% 
  count(cigarette_use)

#> Complete
#> Billed: 14.68 MB
#> Downloading 3 rows in 1 pages.
#> # Source:   lazy query [?? x 2]
#> # Database: BigQueryConnection
#>   cigarette_use         n
#>   <lgl>             <int>
#> 1 FALSE           1426713
#> 2 NA            123796721
#> 3 FALSE          12603329

title: treatment of INT64
description:
Since R works with 32 bit integers, currently 64 bit integers parsed by bigrquery's new low-level API are converted into NA/-1/other without warnings, unlike the previous query_exec treatment.

Some examples:

```
# same output for largest 32 bit integer
query <- "
SELECT 2147483647 as integer
;
"
bq_table_download(bq_project_query(project, query))
query_exec(query,project=project)

# similar output for largest 32 bit int + 1
query <- "
SELECT 2147483647+1 as integer
;
"

bq_table_download(bq_project_query(project, query))
query_exec(query,project=project)

# differing output for largest 32 bit int + 5
query <- "
SELECT 2147483647+5 as integer
;
"

bq_table_download(bq_project_query(project, query))
query_exec(query,project=project)

# differing output for largest 64 bit int
query <- "
SELECT 9223372036854775807 as integer
;
"

bq_table_download(bq_project_query(project, query))
query_exec(query,project=project)
```

title: FR: provide one function for query + wait + download
description:
as far as I understand not counting deprecated functions you can only download the result of a query in two steps: first call `bq_project_query` and than `bq_table_download` I believe these two after each other are such a common case that it would be worth to offer a shortcut

previously `query_exec` did all this

title: show query running time after completion in console
description:
in previous version , query exec showed running time like `Running job -: 38s` even after finishing which is useful to inform yourself (ie you might do sg else waiting for a longer query then return after a longer time and want to know what time it actually took)

this is relevant for `bq_project_query`

this would be a nice-to-have, definitely not a must-have

title: Making print a bigquery tbl more efficient
description:
Particularly for tables - we don't need to do the full query.

This likely needs a `collect.tbl_BigQueryConnection`

title: Only ever evaluate a query once per tbl
description: Printing a tbl currently forces bigquery to compute the entire query and cache it to a temporary table. So we might as well use an object with reference semantics to capture this.

description:
```
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(bigrquery)

con_us <- DBI::dbConnect(
  dbi_driver(),
  project = "bigquery-public-data",
  dataset = "utility_us",
  billing = "profound-ranger-99202"
)

x <- tbl(con_us, sql("SELECT * FROM utility_eu.country_code_iso"))
```

(Part of #101)

title: Function to load a table from Google Cloud Storage object(s)?
description:
BQ allows [loading data directly from cloud storage](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/loading-data-cloud-storage). Currently `bigrquery` has a `insert_upload_job` function that writes a temp csv file from a data frame and loads the temp csv into a BQ table. Can we also have a function to load a table from one or many objects in Cloud Storage?  I think it can be done by using a simple `POST` to `https://www.googleapis.com/bigquery/v2/` with a `configuration.load` payload specifying the meta information.

Is someone already working on this feature? If not, I can take a stab and send out a pull request.

title: pmin() and pmax() translation to SQL
description:
Currently `pmax()` and `pmin()` are translated to `MIN()` and `MAX()` respectively, via [`dbplyr::base_scalar`](https://github.com/tidyverse/dbplyr/blob/master/R/translate-sql-base.r#L142).

```
  pmin = sql_prefix("min"),
  pmax = sql_prefix("max"),
```

This is problematic for BigQuery because [`MAX()`](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/functions-and-operators#max) and [`MIN()`](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/functions-and-operators#min) only accepts a single expression as argument.

A better translation is [`GREATEST()` and `LEAST()`](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/functions-and-operators#mathematical-functions) that accepts multiple expressions as arguments.

title: Window function translation to SQL
description:
Currently `sd()`, `all()` and `any()` window functions are translated to SQL using [the following snippet](https://github.com/rstats-db/bigrquery/blob/master/R/dplyr.r#L108).

```r
    dbplyr::sql_translator(
      .parent = dbplyr::base_win,
      sd = dbplyr::win_recycled("sd"),
      all = dbplyr::win_recycled("all"),
      any = dbplyr::win_recycled("any"),
      ...
    )
```

This produces wrong SQL translation as `sd()` should be translated to `STDDEV_SAMP()`; `all()` to `LOGICAL_AND()` and `any()` to `LOGICAL_OR()`.

Furthermore, BigQuery doesn't support `OVER()` clause for `LOGICAL_AND()` and `LOGICAL_OR()`. So `all()` and `any()` should be translated using `win_absent()` instead.

title: Support use of `fields`, and use it to minimize data transfer for some paging/polling operations.
description:
(This is an offshoot of #58.)

List operations in the BQ API generally return all information about each object by default -- for trying to examine lists of objects, this is great. However, if we're (say) polling for job completion, or looking for a specific table/dataset, it's often wasteful to pull all the data every time. (In particular, it's annoying for manual investigation/debugging.)

IWBN to use `fields` (which is a global query param in the API) to reduce the set of fields we're pulling: [docs](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/api-performance#partial-response).

description:
I have a table with 128 columns and about 10,000 rows in bigquery.  In R Studio running on a Google Cloud instance, I have been assigning the result of a query to a variable with:
```
tm_orig <- query_exec("SELECT *
  FROM my_dataset.my_table
;
", project='my-project');
```

This has worked for the past few weeks with no problems.  Today, I received the error:
```
0 bytes processed
Error: Internal Error
```

Solution:
If we change page_size to a smaller value (default is 10,000) the query succeeds, supposedly because results are spread across multiple page requests, and whatever (possibly memory issue?) is causing the internal error is not triggered.  I'm skeptical as to whether it's a system memory issue, because I can continue to assign values to other variables in R Studio with no problems.  It seems like there is an issue with iterating through the pages in the response.

If this paging exception were caught, outputting a "decrease page_size" suggestion might help others.

title: Have default project?
Allow for cross-dataset interactions in the dplyr backend
description:
The `src_bigquery` function in `bigrquery` takes in a `dataset` argument, which specifies which dataset tables are accessed from. 

While this is, of course, required in order to specify a table, there is no reason that when tables are joined or otherwise compared across datasets in the same project that there needs to be copying of one table into the other dataset. 

I suggest that `src_bigquery` ought to allow for the input of either a particular dataset _or_ an entire project, in which case `tbl` can source from any table in any dataset in the project. Provided that the subsequent queries use the fully-qualified table names (e.g. `publicdata.natality` as opposed to just `natality`), there should not be any problems.

This is a current issue for me: I have a project which looks like:
- Dataset 1
  - Table A
- Dataset 2
  - Table B 

If I want to access these using `dplyr` and join them then I'd do something like 

``` R
ds.1 <- src_bigquery("project", "dataset1")
ds.2 <- src_bigquery("project", "dataset2")
tb.A <- tbl(ds.1, "tablea")
tb.B <- tbl(ds.2, "tableb")
tb.joined <- tb.A %>% inner_join(tb.B, by = "col")
```

This would throw an error:
 `Error: x and y don't share the same src. Set copy = TRUE to copy y into x's source (this may be time consuming).`

However, this is not necessary, as datasets across projects are allowed to access each other. I'd like to avoid the copying in this scenario. 

That is (as in, say, MySQL) the following query would work just fine: 

``` SQL
SELECT * FROM 
project::dataset1.tablea as tbl_a 
INNER JOIN 
project::dataset2.tableb as tbl_b
ON  tbl_a.col = tbl_b.col
```

title: responseTooLarge reason is not output in R/request.r::signal_reason()
description:
When querying a table that contains many fields, I will occasionally receive the ambiguous output:

`Internal Error`

An example:
```
  SELECT *
      FROM `bigquery-public-data.samples.github_timeline`
```


The issue occurs in `R/request.r`: results are retrieved from `bq_get`, which calls httr `GET` and finally `process_request`.  The error that arises from `process_request` is passed to `R/request.r::signal_reason`, which signals a condition, but since this condition isn't handled, `signal_reason` ends with:
```
stop(message, call. = FALSE)
```

Unfortunately, the `message` output is uninformative, it only contains "Internal Error".  Helpful information is contained in `reason`.  In this case, it contains  `responseTooLarge`.

This specific issue can be solved by reducing the page_size argument, however my point is that `reason` contains additional information that is useful for troubleshooting.  Outputting `reason` and not just `message` in `R/request::signal_reason.r` would be helpful.

Another option is to handle the bigrquery_responseTooLarge class condition that is signaled, perhaps with a message recommending a smaller page_size argument.

title: `all()` translation to SQL
description:
Currently `all()` is translated into `LOGICAL_ANY()` via [this snippet](https://github.com/rstats-db/bigrquery/blob/master/R/dplyr.r#L106) in `dplyr.r`.

```r
dbplyr::sql_translator(.parent = dbplyr::base_agg,
      ...
      all = sql_prefix("LOGICAL_ANY", 1)
    ),
```

The issue is that there's no `LOGICAL_ANY()` function in BigQuery. It should be [`LOGICAL_AND()`](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/functions-and-operators#logical_and).

title: `%||%` translation to SQL
description:
Currently `dplyr.r` has [this snippet](https://github.com/rstats-db/bigrquery/blob/master/R/dplyr.r#L100) to translate `%||%` function.

```r
dbplyr::sql_translator(.parent = dbplyr::base_agg,
      ...
      "%||%" = sql_prefix("concat"),
      ...)
```

This has two issues:

1. `%||%` should be a scalar function, not an aggregate function. Its parent should be `dbplyr::base_scalar`.
2. `%||%` shouldn't be translated into `concat()`. [`IFNULL()`](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/functions-and-operators#conditional-expressions) is probably a better translation.

The fix is rather straightforward. I can send out a PR to fix this if necessary.

title: dplyr backend for BigQuery: Get resulting schema for a query before executing it
description:
Per @hadley, he was looking for a way to get the result schema for a particular query _prior_ to executing it.

Unfortunately the BigQuery API does not support this today.  Per advice from @fhoffa:
1. Filing a [feature request](https://code.google.com/p/google-bigquery/issues/entry?template=Feature%20Request) to the BigQuery team to support this cleanly would be most appreciated.
2. In the meantime, [table decorators](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/table-decorators) can be used to _effectively_ run a query on zero bytes of data.  By adding @-1- to the end of the table name, it will access everything that has been loaded in the last millisecond.  _Note that if any data was actually loaded within the prior millisecond the result would operate over more than zero bytes, but this should do the trick the vast majority of the time._

title: change from integer to numeric conversion?
description:
Since bigquery seems to like using unix timestamps in milliseconds (at least that's how we set it up, but also many of the bigquery time functions deal with msecs), and since R integers are limited to 32 bits (and since it's not 1970 anymore) I'm wondering if changing the conversion in extract_data to use as.numeric would be a good idea.

Part of the problem here is due to an inconsistency with how as.integer works. The man page states that:

> The answer will be ‘NA’ unless the coercion succeeds.  Real
> values larger in modulus than the largest integer are coerced to
> ‘NA’ (unlike S which gives the most extreme integer of the same
> sign). 

But it turns out that as.integer('1414040723000') returns 2^31 - 1 instead of NA (applying as.numeric first returns NA).

It seems like this is a problematic failure mode - if you see a column of NAs, you realize something failed, whereas a column of maxint is less clearly wrong.

Of course there are lots of workarounds - I was just surprised by this behavior.

title: Dangerous bug with `filter` sql translations
description:
Hello everyone! It is great to see that `bigrquery` is getting under developers' spotlight again! 
If you don't mind I will be rolling out some of the issues that I ran into (some are pretty dangerous) over the year of working with it in my personal fork.

Below is the first dangerous bug.

``` r
library(dplyr)
library(bigrquery)

BILLING_PROJECT <- "<YOUR_BILLING_PROJECT>"
BILLING_DATASET <- "<DATASET_INSIDE_THAT_PROJECT>"

bq <- src_bigquery(BILLING_PROJECT, BILLING_DATASET)

# Upload the simple test data frame to your project
df <- data.frame(a = 1:100, b = 1:100)

bq_df <- copy_to(bq, df, name = "bq_df")

bq_df %>%
  filter(a == 1L | a== 2L) %>%
  filter(b == 100L) %>% 
  explain
```

It appears that two consecutive `filter`s produce an incorrect logical expression:

``` sql
<SQL>
SELECT [a], [b]
FROM [bq_df]
WHERE [a] = 1 OR [a] = 2 AND [b] = 100
```

Indeed, the code will report 1 incorrect record back

``` r
bq_df %>%
  filter(a == 1L | a== 2L) %>%
  filter(b == 100L) %>%
  collect()
```

which gives us

``` r
Source: local data frame [1 x 2]
      a     b
  (int) (int)
1     1     1
```

While using regular data frames:

``` r
df %>%
  filter(a == 1L | a== 2L) %>%
  filter(b == 100L)
```

the answer is correct:

``` r
[1] a b
<0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
```

I think I solved it by requiring a collapse after every `filter` in the same spirit as #55.

If this is considered an acceptable solution, I can submit a pull request similar to #55 fixing it.

title: httr update to 1.0.0 breaks tbl()
description:
Hello,

Recent update of httr to [1.0.0](https://github.com/hadley/httr/commit/485d387daffcd76aca454fad74b7b16bafd30acd) switched `httr` to `curl` instead of `RCurl`. 

This update breaks the basic functionality of `bigrquery` at the very least with respect to `tbl` function. In order to confirm, please update to `httr 1.0.0` and run the following to confirm:

``` r
library(dplyr)
library(bigrquery)

BILLING_PROJECT <- "<YOUR_BILLING_PROJECT>"
BILLING_DATASET <- "<DATASET_INSIDE_THAT_PROJECT>"

bq <- src_bigquery(BILLING_PROJECT, BILLING_DATASET)

# Upload the test data frame to your project
df <- data.frame(a = 1:100, b = 101:200)
httr_issue <- copy_to(bq, df, name = "httr_issue")

httr_issue2 <- bq %>% tbl("httr_issue")
```

which will produce the following error if `httr` is version 1.0.0:

``` r
Error in curl::curl_escape(names(url$query)) : 
  `url` must be a character vector.
```

and will work correctly if `httr` is `0.6.1`.

The issue is caused by difference in behavior of curlEscape with NULLs for `curl` vs `RCurl`. Note that `curl::curl_escape(NULL)` results in an error while `RCurl::curlEscape` produces an empty vector.

``` r
> curl::curl_escape(NULL)
Error in curl::curl_escape(NULL) :
    `url` must be a character vector.
> RCurl::curlEscape(NULL)
character(0)
```

As of now, the quick fix is to downgrade `httr` back to `v0.6.1`:

``` r
devtools::install_github("hadley/httr@v0.6.1")
```

title: Using local credentials
description:
Hey there Hadley, 

Another way to use BigQuery without going to Google's webapp is by using [bq](https://developers.google.com/bigquery/docs/cli_tool).

With `bq`, you basically locally save a file `~/.bigquery.v2.token` which in the latest version (doesn't seem documented on Google's side) is nothing more than a `json` configuration file containing your OAuth2 credentials (tokens, user-agent, etc).

The second file of interest that one needs to have when using `bq` is `~/.bigqueryrc` which contains the default project id ( **billing_id** for `query_exec(...)`), and the aforementioned token file.

Now, when those files are present, would you be interested in seeing the web-authentication replaced by those files? The flow would be quite simple:

```
If ~/.bigquery.rc exists:
    use content for authentication
    If authentication() fails:
        go to Web-Browser authentication
 Else default to web-browser authentication()
```

title: auth is only storing access token not refresh token
description: From what I can tell, bigrquery auth doesn't store the oauth2 refresh token, just the access token. The access token is only valid for a brief amount of time, which means you need to re-authorize periodically. If you store the refresh token, you shouldn't have to re-authorize.

title: bigrquery needs to update token handling for httr changes
description:

I'm starting to do this now -- opening this issue for tracking.
